blocks.why: Full night in before a 14h32 four-sector day — up at 07:45 local to leave the door at 08:50 for an 08:00Z report.
Only six hours available after a 00:32 local block-in, so get straight to bed and don't touch a phone on the drive home.
First proper recovery night of the month — pay back the short one before the two days off.
Normal home night, stay anchored on Madrid time.
Bank a full night before the Singapore night crossing.
Ninety minutes before a 12:45Z report on a duty that runs right through my body night — this nap is what carries me to top of descent.
Straight into the hotel bed on arrival to clear the all-night sector, then get up in the Singapore afternoon.
Stay on Madrid time for a 26-hour layover — this is 04:00–12:00 local Singapore, and it lines me up for a 14:45 local pick-up.
Home just after 01:00 local off a 15h20 duty — sleep as long as the body will take it.
Early to bed for an 08:00 local sim/ground start; alarm at 06:00 local for the 70-minute run in.
Sleep in the evening after training because the next report is 02:00 local — treat this as the night, blackout blinds and no dinner too late.
Short sleep after a duty that ran straight through the WOCL, but set an alarm so I can still sleep tonight.
Re-anchor to Madrid nights on the day off.
Full night before the Dubai out-and-back pairing.
Into the hotel around 02:00 local Dubai — this is midnight to 07:30 body time, so it sleeps like a normal night.
Afternoon nap before a 21:50 local report and a red-eye back to Madrid landing at 04:10 local.
Home at dawn off the night flight — sleep the morning, but be up by lunchtime or I'll never get down early tonight.
Lights out at 21:00 local for a 06:10 local report — the alarm is 04:00 local and this sleep will not come easily, so protect the wind-down.
Nine hours before the Bogotá sector; I want to leave home with a full tank for a 10h15 westbound.
Short nap on arrival in the Bogotá afternoon to bridge to a local bedtime instead of collapsing at 15:00.
First real Bogotá night, 22:00–06:00 local — with 54 hours here it's worth shifting onto local time.
Second local night to consolidate the shift before the night departure.
Long afternoon sleep, 13:00–18:30 local, because the report is 20:30 local and I'll be awake until Madrid mid-afternoon.
A controlled two and a half hours on getting home — enough to take the edge off without stealing tonight's sleep.
Snap back onto Madrid nights; the 13:15 local report tomorrow gives me room to do it properly.
Home at 05:00 local after a 14h38 duty — sleep the morning on the day off.
Bed at 20:30 local for a 06:10 local report; short notice on the body clock, so accept a broken sleep and top up later.
Five and a half hours in the middle of the day is the whole plan for tonight — the second duty is an all-nighter reporting 21:15 local.
Morning sleep between two night duties — curtains shut, phone off, and up in time to eat before an 18:35 local departure from home.
Same again after the second night; six hours is all the gap allows before a 16:00Z report.
First sleep after three nights on the trot — take it long, this is the recovery sleep the block needs.
Second recovery night to get fully back on Madrid time before standby.
Normal night after an uneventful afternoon standby.
Bed at 20:00 local so I'm actually awake and callable when standby opens at 05:00 local.
Non-negotiable afternoon sleep between standby release and a 21:00 local report for four night sectors.
Home just after 07:30 local off the last night duty — sleep it out, nothing to get up for.
Back onto a normal night on the first clear day off.
Finish the month on home time so October starts from a clean baseline.

conflicts.statement: Two separate duties are printed against 10SEP and they overlap completely: a MAD-DUB-MAD-FCO-MAD pairing reporting 00:00Z and finishing 13:55Z, and a MAD-ARN-MAD-ARN-MAD pairing reporting 23:55Z on 09SEP and finishing 19:53Z. Flight number CV110 also appears in both with different sectors. Only one of these can be flown; I have planned sleep around the first (00:00Z report).
options: Call crewing before the 09SEP training day and get written confirmation of which pairing stands
If it turns out to be the 19h58 ARN pairing, the whole 09-10SEP sleep plan moves and the duty needs a fatigue risk assessment before acceptance
Ask for the roster to be republished with the duplicate removed so the rest of the month's rest calculations are trustworthy

conflicts.statement: The second 10SEP entry shows a 19h58 duty with four sectors starting at 23:55Z. That is far beyond any single-crew FDP I have seen and it swallows the whole window of circadian low.
options: Treat it as a printing error until crewing confirms otherwise
If it is real, decline on fatigue grounds and file the report
Ask whether it was meant to be split into two duties with a rest period

conflicts.statement: Training on 09SEP ends 14:00Z and the 10SEP report is 00:00Z — 10h00 at home base, and the commute takes 2h20 of that round trip, leaving roughly 7h30 of actual sleep opportunity before a duty that runs all night.
options: Ask for the 10SEP report to be moved later or the training day to finish earlier
Take the 15:45–22:00Z evening sleep as planned and treat it as the main sleep, not a nap
Raise a fatigue report if the pairing stands as rostered

conflicts.statement: Two duties on 22SEP: the early finishes 09:13Z and the next reports 19:15Z. That is 10h02 apart, minus 2h20 of commuting, and the second duty is a full night through to 07:42Z.
options: Request the two 22SEP duties be split across different days
Protect the 11:00–16:30Z nap absolutely — no errands, no daylight
Ask for hotel accommodation near MAD between the duties to recover the commute time

conflicts.statement: Three back-to-back night duties: 22SEP 19:15Z–23SEP 07:42Z, 23SEP 17:45Z–24SEP 05:58Z, and 24SEP 16:00Z–25SEP 02:03Z, each separated by only about 10 hours at home. Every one of them works through 02:00–06:00 body time and there is no chance to recover between them.
options: Ask crewing to break the run with a day off after the 23SEP duty
Plan for daytime sleep in a fully darkened room and accept reduced quality — expect to be at your worst on the last night
File a fatigue report covering the block regardless of outcome, so the pattern is visible

conflicts.statement: Off duty 07:42Z on 23SEP, report 17:45Z the same day — 10h03, which is a daytime sleep opportunity only.
options: Request a later report on 23SEP
Sleep 09:15–15:30Z with blackout and eye mask; do not try to stay awake through the morning
Discuss with the operator whether this counts as a reduced rest period requiring augmentation

conflicts.statement: The DXB return blocks in at 02:10Z on 14SEP and the 15SEP duty reports 04:10Z, which is a 04:00 local alarm. The 14SEP day off is spent recovering from a night flight and immediately re-shifting for an early — sleep on the night of 14/15SEP will be short and fragmented.
options: Ask for the 15SEP report to be moved back if the FCO rotation allows
Split sleep as planned: morning recovery on 14SEP, then a 21:00 local bedtime
Consider an airport hotel on the night of 14/15SEP to recover the 70-minute commute

conflicts.statement: Standby runs 03:00–09:00Z on 28SEP and a four-sector night duty reports 19:00Z the same day, ending 04:26Z. That is 10h between them, and if the standby is called out the day gets very long very quickly.
options: Ask crewing whether the standby can be released early if uncalled
Take the 11:00–16:00Z nap as a hard requirement, not an option
If called out from the standby, notify crewing immediately that the 19:00Z report is at risk on fatigue grounds

conflicts.statement: The roster gives standby only as MAD-MAD with an end time and a duration; it does not say whether it is home standby or airport standby, and it does not print a start time. I derived 26SEP 11:00–17:00Z and 28SEP 03:00–09:00Z by subtracting the duration from the off-duty time.
options: Confirm the standby type with crewing — a 03:00Z airport standby on 28SEP means leaving home at 01:50Z
Confirm the callout response time so the pre-standby sleep can be sized correctly
If it is airport standby on 28SEP, move the 27/28SEP sleep earlier by 60–90 minutes

conflicts.statement: The 05SEP and 07SEP Singapore duties are 15h20 each and the 16SEP/19SEP Bogotá duties are 12h05 each. These only work with augmented crew and in-flight bunk rest, which the roster does not state.
options: Confirm crew complement and rest facility class before the trip
Agree the in-flight rest split at briefing — take the second rest on the eastbound SIN-MAD and the last rest on BOG-MAD so you land alert
If it is a two-pilot operation, query it with crewing before report

conflicts.statement: The 19SEP Bogotá return is dated 19SEP with a 02:50Z departure, so the 01:30Z report falls on 18SEP at 20:30 local Bogotá. Anyone reading the roster in local time could turn up a day late.
options: Set the hotel wake-up and the alarm against local Bogotá time, on the evening of 18SEP
Confirm the pick-up time with the crew hotel on arrival, not on the day
Cross-check the transport booking against the 18SEP evening, not 19SEP
